question.text:
The family of recursive languages is closed under

  1. Union
  2. Intersection
  3. Reversal
  1. (i) and (ii) only          
  2. (ii) and (iii) only
  3. (i) and (iii) only
  4. (i), (ii) and (iii)

Which of the following problems is/are undecidable? Whether the language accepted by a Turing Machine is

  1. Empty
  2. Finite
  3. Regular
  4. Context free
  1. (i) & (iii) only
  2. (ii) only
  3. (i) & (iv) only
  4. All

$L = \{B(N)\#B(N+1) \mid B(N)$ represents binary pattern for given $N.$ Example $B(5)=101, N\geq 1\}.$ Then which of the following is true for $L?$

  1. $L$ is Regular
  2. $L$ is Context-free but not Regular
  3. $L$ is Recursive but not Context-free
  4. $L$ is Recursive enumerable but not Recursive

Which of the following statements is correct?

  1. Regular languages are closed under infinite union
  2. Context free languages are closed under intersection
  3. Regular languages are closed under substitution
  4. Context free languages are not closed under substitution

Consider the following statements:

  1. $A_{TM} = \{ \langle M,W \rangle \mid \text{ M is a TM and M accepts W}\}\text{ is undecidable}.$
  2. A language $L$ is decidable if both $L$ and $\bar{L}$  are Turing – recognizable

Which of the above statement(s) is/are true?

  1. Only I
  2. Only II
  3. Both I and II
  4. None of the above

Match the following statements with true (T) / false (F)

  •  S1 : Complement of a CFL need not be recursive
  •  S2 : If $L$ is recursive then $\bar L$ is also recursive
  •  S3 : If $L_1$ is recursive and $L_2$ is recursive enumerable then $L_2-L_1$ need not be recursive enumerable
  •  S4 : Recursive sets are closed under complementation and substitution
  1. $\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline S_1 & T \\ \hline S_2 & F \\ \hline S_3 & T \\ \hline S_4 & F \\ \hline \end{array}$
  2. $\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline S_1 & T \\ \hline S_2 & F \\ \hline S_3 & F \\ \hline S_4 & T \\ \hline \end{array}$
  3. $\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline S_1 & F \\ \hline S_2 & T \\ \hline S_3 & T \\ \hline S_4 & F \\ \hline \end{array}$
  4. $\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline S_1 & F \\ \hline S_2 & T \\ \hline S_3 & F \\ \hline S_4 & F \\ \hline \end{array}$

Match the following statements with True (T) / False (F)

  • $ S_1 : ALL_{CFG} = \{ \langle G \rangle \mid \text{G is a CFG and } L(G) = \Sigma^* \} \text{ is undecidable}$
  • $ S_2 :A = \{ \langle G \rangle \mid \text{ G is a CFG over } \{0,1\}^{*}, 1^{*} \cap L(G) \neq \phi \} \text{ is undecidable}$
  • $ S_3 : E_{CFG} = \{ \langle G,G^{'} \rangle \mid  G, G^{'}\text{ are CFG's and L(G) = L(G') }\} \text{ is undecidable}$
  • $ S_4 : EM_{CFG} = \{ \langle G \rangle \mid \text{ G is a CFG and }L(G) = \phi\} \text{ is decidable}$
  1. $S_1 - T,  \; S_2 - F, \;S_3 - T, \; S_4 - T$
  2. $S_1 - T, \; S_2 - T, \; S_3 - T, \; S_4 - T$
  3. $S_1 - F, \; S_2 - F, \; S_3 - T, \; S_4 - T$
  4. $S_1 - F, \; S_2 - T, \; S_3 - T, \; S_4 - T$

Which of the following statement is TRUE about the given Turing Machine transitions below?

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline \delta&0&1&B \\ \hline q_0 &(q_1, 0, R)& (q_1, 1, R) & \text{HALT} \\ \hline 
q_1 &(q_0, 0, R)& (q_0, 1, R) & (q_f, B, R) \\ \hline
q_f & \text{HALT}& \text{HALT} & \text{HALT} \\ \hline
 \end{array}$$

where $ \tau = \{ 0,1,B \} \\ Q = \{ q_{0}, q_{1}, q_{f}\} \\ F = \{ q_{f}\} \\ \text{Initial} = q_{0}$

  1. TM does not halt on any string starting with $'1'$      
  2. TM halts on all strings of odd length and accept it
  3. TM does not halt on any string in $\Sigma ^{*}$   
  4. None of these

Which of the following statements is FALSE with respect to Recursive enumerable languages?
  1. Recursive enumerable languages are closed under kleene closure operation
  2. Recursive enumerable languages are closed under Intersection
  3. If $L$ is recursive enumerable then complement of $L$ is also recursive enumerable
  4. Recursive enumerable languages are not closed under set difference

Consider the following languages:

  • $L_1 = \{w \mid w \in \{a,b,c\}^*, n_a(w)=n_b(w)=n_c(w)\}$ 
  • $L_2 = \{wvw^{R}: w,v \in \{a,b\}^{+}, \mid w \mid \geq \mid v \mid \}$

Which of the following is/are true?

  1. $L_1$ is CSL and $L_2$ is CFL
  2. Both $L_1$ and $L_2$ are CSL
  3. Neither $L_1$ nor $L_2$ is CSL
  4. $L_1$ is CFL and $L_2$ is CSL

Consider two languages, $L_1$ and $L_2$ defined over same alphabet set $\Sigma.$ Let $L_1 \oplus L_2= $$\{w \mid \text{ w belongs to exactly one out of } L_1 \text{ and } L_2\}$. Suppose $L_1$ is regular and $L_2$ is context-free, then which of the following statements is TRUE?

  1. $L_1 \oplus L_2 \text{ is not recursive}$
  2. $L_1 \oplus L_2 \text{ is context-free but not necessarily regular}$
  3. $L_1 \oplus L_2 \text{ is regular}$
  4. $L_1 \oplus L_2 \text{ is recursive but not necessarily context-free}$

Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?

  1. If $L$ is decidable, $L^{R}$ may or may not be decidable.
  2. If $L\subseteq \{0\}^{*}$, then $L$ is decidable
  3. If $ L \leq_m\{ 0^{n} 1^{n} \mid n \geq 0\}$, then L is decidable
  1. (i) – True, (ii) – True, (iii) – False
  2. (i) – True, (ii) – False, (iii) – False
  3. (i) – False, (ii) – False, (iii) – True
  4. (i) – False, (ii) – True, (iii) – True

Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?

  1. If $L_1,L_2 \in \Sigma^{*}$ and both $L_1$ and $L_2$ are infinite, then $L_1 \cap L_2$ is also infinite
  2. If $L \subseteq \Sigma^{*}$ is an infinite language, then $\text{Complement}(L)$ is finite.
  1. I – False, II – True
  2. I –True , II – False
  3. Both I and II are True
  4. Both I and II are False

Which of the following is/are TRUE?

  1. If $L_1$ is context free and $L_2$ is not context free, then $L_1 L_2$ is not context free.
  2. If $L_1$ is context free and $L_2$ is not context free, then $L_1 L_2$ is context free.
  3. If $L_1$ and $L_2$ are context free, then $L_1 \cap L_2$ is not context free.
  4. If a language $L$ is context free then $L'$ is Turing decidable.
  1. (i) – F, (ii) – T, (iii) – T, (iv) – F
  2. (i) – F, (ii) – F, (iii) – F, (iv) – F
  3. (i) – F, (ii) – F, (iii) – F, (iv) – T
  4. (i) – T, (ii) – F, (iii) – T, (iv) – T

Let $L=\{x \mid x \in (0+1)^{*} , \text{ if } x_i \text{(bit at } i^{th} \text{ position of x) }=1$ $ \text{ then each of the next } 2^i \text{ positions must be a 1}\}$ then $L$ is?

  1. Regular
  2. CFL but not regular
  3. CSL but not CFL
  4. Recursive but not CSL
